newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Wood & Co launches WIF-20 to track Czech funds.
newsitem.headline: Wood & Co launches WIF-20 to track Czech funds.

text.p: Prague-based brokerage house Wood & Company said on Tuesday it had launched a new daily index, the WIF-20, to track the performance of the top Czech investment funds.

In a statement, the firm said that since Monday its Wood Index Funds, or WIF-20, had been measuring the 20 largest funds and unit trusts traded on the Prague Stock Exchange ranked by market capitalisation.
"(The index) is based on International Finance Corporation methodology applied to emerging markets," it said.
"The flexibility of the index methodology allows it to reflect sudden changes such as stock mergers, stock splits, the addition of a new fund to the index, etc."
Funds which have been converted into holding companies were excluded from the index.
The index has a base of 1,000 points, and proportions of the index will change as funds' market capitalisation changes.
Total market capitalisation of the index is $1.52 billion or more than 80 percent of the market value of all Czech funds.

The 20 index components -- of which the RIF, SPIF Cesky, and KB IF funds comprise 55.2 percent of the index base -- control net assets totalling $2.88 billion, or about 20 percent of the entire Czech equities market.
Wood said the component funds are trading at a weighted average discount of 42.94 percent to net asset value.

A 1996 comparison of the funds in the WIF-20 with the HN-Wood index, which measures the 60 most capitalised issues on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) and excludes funds, shows the funds underperforming the top shares on the market.

The HN-Wood index, the oldest measure of the renascent PSE, gained 26.63 percent in 1996 while the WIF-20 components would have shown an absolute drop for the year of 5.7 percent, when retroactively applied.
In relative terms, the funds underperformed the HN-Wood stocks by 25.53 percent.
